Fit the final model after nested cross-validation

Source: R/nested-final-fit.R
nested_final_fit.Rd

nested_final_fit() fits the model to deploy after a nested run. It runs the same procedure (tune, select, fit) once more on all the data.

Usage

nested_final_fit(object, results, ..., id = NULL)

Arguments

object

The workflows::workflow() the nested run used, or a nested_results_set from nested_workflow_map() with id naming the workflow to fit. After a run on a model specification, pass workflows::workflow(preprocessor, spec).

results

The nested_results from nested_tune_grid(), another nested tuning function or nested_fit_resamples(). The tuner and its arguments, the metrics, eval_time and the selection rule are read from it.

...

Not used, and must be empty.

id

For a nested_results_set, the wflow_id of the workflow to fit. Leave results missing then.

Value

An object of class nested_final_fit with these elements:

  • workflow, the trained workflow. The object answers predict() and augment() directly.

  • selected, the parameters chosen, and tuning, the tuning run they were chosen from.

  • tuning_seed and fit_seed, the two seeds that reproduce it.

  • procedure, the settings of the run, as results holds them.

Where nothing was tuned, selected is an empty table and tuning is NULL.

Details

The function rebuilds the inner resamples on all the rows from the design's inside specification. It tunes with the same tuner and settings, picks a candidate with the same selection_rule(), and fits the finalized workflow on all the data. A parameter range that depends on the data is finalized on all the rows. The outer folds and their choices play no part. Where nothing was tuned, the function only fits the workflow on all the data.

The design keeps inside as a call, and this function evaluates it again in the environment you call from. Write it with literal arguments, such as vfold_cv(v = 5). With vfold_cv(v = k), another k in scope gives another design.

A workflow whose model or preprocessor differs from the one the nested run used is an error, and the message names the first part that differs. Model arguments and recipe functions are compared as written. So a name bound to another value is not caught, and neither is a function with the same body that uses other values. A run in which some folds failed is still fitted. To fit one workflow of a set, pass the set as object, name the workflow with id, and leave results missing.

What to report

The nested estimate describes the procedure that produced this model, not this model itself. Report collect_metrics() on results as the estimate for this model, because the model comes from the same procedure. It averages over what each fold chose, so it says nothing about the setting this model carries. It describes new data drawn like your training data. If the outer folds chose different parameters, report that too.

For a workflow from a set, report that workflow's rows only if you chose the workflow before you saw the set's estimates. A choice made from those estimates is a selection the outer loop did not nest.

Do not report the metrics in the tuning element. They come from the resamples that chose the candidate, so they are optimistic on average. The nested estimate tends to be slightly pessimistic instead, because each outer fold trained on fewer rows. vignette("estimate") gives the sizes measured in two studies.

Reproducibility

Call set.seed() before the function. It draws two seeds: the first builds the inner resamples and tunes, and the second fits. Both are kept on the object, and your random state is restored on exit. So two calls with no set.seed() between them give the same model, as repeated tune::tune_grid() calls do. nested_tune_grid() says what an R-side seed cannot pin.

The code below redoes the fit by hand. The values come from extract_procedure(), except metrics, which is attr(results, "metrics"), and data, the data the design was built on. Only the tuning line changes with the tuner.

set.seed(fit$tuning_seed, kind = "Mersenne-Twister",
         normal.kind = "Inversion", sample.kind = "Rejection")
inner <- <the design's `inside` specification>(data)
control <- extract_procedure(fit)$control
# Run the one tuning line for the recorded tuner.
# Grid search and the races use the control as it is.
tuned <- tune_grid(object, inner, grid = grid, param_info = param_info,
  metrics = metrics, eval_time = eval_time, control = control)
tuned <- tune_race_anova(object, inner, grid = grid, param_info = param_info,
  metrics = metrics, eval_time = eval_time, control = control)
tuned <- tune_race_win_loss(object, inner, grid = grid, param_info = param_info,
  metrics = metrics, eval_time = eval_time, control = control)
# So does annealing.
tuned <- tune_sim_anneal(object, inner, iter = iter, initial = initial,
  param_info = param_info, metrics = metrics, eval_time = eval_time,
  control = control)
# A Bayesian search also sets the control's seed.
control$seed <- fit$tuning_seed
tuned <- tune_bayes(object, inner, iter = iter, initial = initial,
  objective = objective, param_info = param_info, metrics = metrics,
  eval_time = eval_time, control = control)
final <- finalize_workflow(object, select_best(tuned, metric = <first metric>))
  # Or select_by_one_std_err() or select_by_pct_loss(), as `select` says.
set.seed(fit$fit_seed, kind = "Mersenne-Twister",
         normal.kind = "Inversion", sample.kind = "Rejection")
fit(final, data)

Where nothing was tuned, the code is fit(object, data) under the second seed.

See also

nested_tune_grid(), nested_tune_bayes(), nested_workflow_map(), predict.nested_final_fit(), extract_workflow()

Examples

data(mtcars)

rec <- recipes::recipe(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars) |>
  recipes::step_pca(recipes::all_predictors(), num_comp = tune::tune())
wf <- workflows::workflow(rec, parsnip::linear_reg())

set.seed(1)
folds <- nested_resamples(
  mtcars,
  outside = rsample::vfold_cv(v = 2),
  inside = rsample::vfold_cv(v = 2)
)
set.seed(2)
res <- nested_tune_grid(wf, folds, grid = data.frame(num_comp = 1:2))
set.seed(3)
final <- nested_final_fit(wf, res)
# The estimate: what the procedure achieves, and the number to report.
collect_metrics(res)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err
#>   <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl>
#> 1 rmse    standard   2.98      2  0.459 
#> 2 rsq     standard   0.747     2  0.0691

# The model: what you deploy.
final
#> 
#> ── Nested cross-validation final fit ──────────────────────────────────
#> Procedure: grid search, 2 candidates scored
#> Selected: num_comp = 1
#> Selecting metric: rmse
#> 
#> ℹ Report the nested estimate from `collect_metrics()` on the results
#>   object this fit was built from. For a fit built from a workflow set,
#>   that is this workflow's rows of `collect_metrics()` on the set. That
#>   holds for a workflow chosen before seeing the set's estimates. It
#>   describes the procedure that produced this model, and it is the
#>   number to report for this model.
#> ℹ Compare the parameters above with `.selected` from that run. Outer
#>   folds choosing differently is selection instability, and it is
#>   information about the procedure rather than noise.
#> ℹ `extract_tune_results()` returns the tuning run selection came from,
#>   and `extract_scored_candidates()` the candidates it scored. Any
#>   metric reachable through the first is a selection-time quantity,
#>   optimistically biased as a claim about this model.

predict(final, new_data = mtcars[1:3, ])
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   .pred
#>   <dbl>
#> 1  23.1
#> 2  23.1
#> 3  25.2
